title: Idempotent stream-resume semantics for metering pipeline
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We've seen production cases where resumed streaming requests (client reconnects / resume) produce overlapping token chunks that get counted twice in the usage pipeline. This primarily impacts customers on per-token billing and quota enforcement. The root cause spans two areas: 1) session resume semantics between the frontend gateway and the runtime where the same tokens are emitted after a reconnection, and 2) the metering pipeline's lack of an idempotency key or canonical dedup criteria for partial-chunk / replayed events.

Scope: implement deterministic, low-latency deduplication for resumed streams at the gateway/runtime boundary and ensure the billing pipeline consumes idempotent events. This ticket covers design, infra changes to the event envelope, runtime gateway changes, and a migration strategy for historical ambiguous records. It does NOT include changes to customer-facing quota UI (handled in a follow-up).

Why this matters: Double-counting leads to incorrect invoices, unexpected quota enforcement, and customer trust issues. For large streaming workloads the cost delta can be significant for individual customers and can trigger automated limited-service fallbacks incorrectly.

Constraints and non-goals: must not add significant per-token latency, cannot rely on perfect clock sync between client and server, must work across reconnects that route to different runtime processes or hosts, and must not change existing billing models (only the measurement path).
acceptance_criteria: Resumed stream events that re-emit overlapping token ranges are deduplicated before they increment customer token counters
Metering event envelope includes an idempotency token and a chunk-range header that uniquely identifies emitted tokens within a stream
No more than 2ms median added latency at the gateway path for non-resumed streams
E2E integration tests that simulate reconnect+replay across host boundaries and validate single-count semantics
Metrics and dashboards updated: percent of resumed streams, deduped events count, and any change in billed tokens vs observed emitted tokens
Runbook appendix with steps to investigate customer disputes and a migration procedure for ambiguous historical windows
proposed_solution: Add a per-stream stable stream_id generated at session start and surfaced through the gateway to runtime and metering. Stream_id persists across reconnects via client-provided session token or server-issued resume_token.

When emitting tokens, attach a chunk_range header: {start_seq, end_seq} relative to stream_id plus a monotonic chunk_sequence number. Include a short idempotency_hash computed over stream_id + start_seq + end_seq.
Metering pipeline sinks dedupe based on (stream_id, idempotency_hash). Events with matching keys within a configurable retention window are dropped before counters are incremented.
Gateway and runtime must persist last-acked end_seq for live sessions in fast key-value store (etcd/redis) to reject immediate replays at the source when possible.

Add a lightweight bloom filter stage in the pipeline for high-throughput, probabilistic early rejection and a strict persistent index for final deduplication to avoid false positives affecting billing.

Backfill/migration: run an offline reconciliation job to locate duplicate pairs in the last 90 days and mark disputed tokens as credits if necessary. Provide a safe rollback toggle for the new dedupe path.

Instrumentation: create counters for dedupe_hits, dedupe_misses, remaining_duplicates, and latency impact. Emit alerts if dedupe rate > 0.1% or if billed tokens drop > 5% compared to baseline over 1h (investigate before auto-action).
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Initial report from billing ops about 3 customer disputes with suspected double-charge on resumed streams. Triage meeting scheduled.
2026-03-04: Spike: validated issue reproducible in staging by simulating reconnects that re-send the last 4 token chunks; confirmed duplicates reach metering topic.
2026-03-07: Design review: agreed on stream_id + chunk_range + idempotency_hash approach. Decision: use ephemeral resume_token that maps to stream_id to avoid exposing internal ids to clients.
2026-03-09: Prototype implemented in gateway to add headers. End-to-end smoke test between gateway and dev-metering showed dedupe working with in-memory index.
2026-03-12: Load test: bloom filter stage reduced write pressure to persistent index by ~78% at 10k concurrent streams. Found pathological case with very long streams requiring index expiry tuning.
2026-03-14: Preparing QA plan and integration tests; drafting migration plan for customer credits. Routing change scheduled behind feature flag for gradual rollout.
